candidates.original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.description: Priming analytic thinking through a scrambled sentence task reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.citation_sentence: Swami et al. (2014) conducted four studies and found that priming analytical thinking reduces belief in well-known conspiracy theories.
candidates.notes: Preregistered direct replication with high statistical power (N=302); Bayesian analyses showed moderate evidence for the null hypothesis; authors explicitly state no evidence that analytic prime reduced conspiracy beliefs. Replication of Study 2 from Swami et al. (2014); no evidence that analytic prime reduced conspiracy beliefs; Bayesian analysis showed moderate evidence for null hypothesis (BF01 = 4.54).

candidates.original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.description: Priming analytic thinking through a disfluent font manipulation reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.citation_sentence: Swami et al. (2014) conducted four studies and found that priming analytical thinking reduces belief in well-known conspiracy theories.
candidates.notes: Preregistered direct replication with high statistical power (N=488); Bayesian analyses showed moderate-to-strong evidence for the null hypothesis; authors explicitly state the original study failed to replicate and no evidence that disfluent font manipulation reduced conspiracy beliefs. Replication of Study 4 from Swami et al. (2014); no evidence that disfluent font manipulation reduced conspiracy beliefs; Bayesian analysis showed moderate-to-strong evidence for null hypothesis (BF01 = 8.20 for GCBS, BF01 = 4.57 for 7/7 conspiracy theories).

candidates.original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.description: In Study 4, presenting questionnaires in a difficult-to-read font to induce analytic thinking was claimed to reduce generic conspiracist beliefs compared with an easy-to-read font condition.
candidates.citation_sentence: This Registered Report aimed to replicate two experimental studies from Swami et al. (2014) which found that priming analytical thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories. Therefore, we decided to replicate Studies 2 and 4 from the original paper.
candidates.notes: The replication tested the Generic Conspiracist Beliefs Scale as one of two outcomes from the original Study 4 and found no significant difference between conditions.

candidates.original_title: Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories
candidates.description: In Study 4, presenting questionnaires in a difficult-to-read font to induce analytic thinking was claimed to reduce belief in conspiracy theories about the 7/7 London bombings compared with an easy-to-read font condition.
candidates.citation_sentence: This Registered Report aimed to replicate two experimental studies from Swami et al. (2014) which found that priming analytical thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories. Therefore, we decided to replicate Studies 2 and 4 from the original paper.
candidates.notes: The replication tested beliefs about 7/7 conspiracy theories as one of two outcomes from the original Study 4 and found no significant difference between conditions.

candidates.citation_sentence: Swami et al. (2014) conducted four studies and found that priming analytical thinking reduces belief in well-known conspiracy theories. Therefore, we decided to replicate Studies 2 and 4 from the original paper.
